target: new: wall of the bearer (endodermal cell walls, part of the bearer, slot 1) + increased thickness (PATO_0000591), thickened on the inner tangential and radial walls
reason: U-type endodermis means the endodermal cell walls are thickened on the inner and side walls, so they look like a U in section. What is thick is the cell wall, so it goes with the wall-as-bearer reading used for thin-walled, not a new term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023 + brown PATO_0000952)
reason: A brown colour at the tip of the tooth or margin, handled like black-tipped and dark-tipped. The apex goes in the part-of-the-bearer slot and brown is the value.

target: new: half-shape (semi- + shape of one half of the bearer: ovate PATO_0001891 [ovoid])
reason: An ovoid cut lengthwise, as on the flat-sided pyrenes and seeds. This is the same half-shape reading as semi-oblong. It is not plain ovoid, and it is not hemispheroid.

target: new: two values of one bearer (depressed FLOPO:0991103 + ovate PATO_0001891 [ovoid])
reason: An ovoid flattened from above, so both values hold. This is the same reading as compressed-ovoid. It is not a range between two shapes.

target: fragmented (PATO_0040047)
reason: Stipules, tunics and stems that break up into pieces as they age. PATO fragmented is explicitly for breaking up during development, unlike broken, which implies injury.

target: pink (PATO_0000954)
reason: A light wash of pink on the part. It is handled like rose-tinged and purple tinged, which were mapped to the plain colour. The faintness is a degree word and does not need a term.

target: new: two values of one bearer (pannose PATO_0104242 + indumentum FLOPO_0986003 white PATO_0000323)
reason: The surface has a felt-like covering (PATO pannose) and the felt is white. The colour belongs to the hairs, not the organ.

target: not papillose (FLOPO:0991059)
reason: Epapillate means without papillae. FLOPO papillose already lists papillate as a synonym, so this is its negation, built the same way as unlobed.

target: new: two values of one bearer (ovate PATO_0001891 [ovoid] + asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: Ovoid with unequal sides, so both values hold. This is the same reading as obliquely ovoid and oblique-obovate.

target: stipitate-glandular (FLOPO:0991172)
reason: Covered with stalked glands whose stalks are short. 'Short' only describes the stalk length, and the quality is still FLOPO stipitate-glandular.

target: tuberous root (PO_0025523)
reason: Most uses are the noun 'tuberoids', the root tubers of orchids, which is a part. The rare adjective use ('roots tuberoid') is FLOPO:0991109 tuberous.

target: approximate (FLOPO:0991190)
reason: Leaves, lobes and spines that sit close to their neighbours without joining them. This is FLOPO approximate, the same as closely set and closely arranged.

target: pink (PATO_0000954)
reason: The colour of the veins, eye or centre is pink. This follows darker brown and darker yellow, and the comparison word is dropped because the other part is not given. Where the location is named (veins, apex), it goes in the part-of-the-bearer slot.

target: not glistening (PATO_0001373)
reason: Lustrous was mapped to PATO glistening (C201), and 'not glossy' became its negation, so 'not lustrous' is the same.

target: obcordate (FLOPO:0991056)
reason: Heart-shaped with the notch at the top, said of the outline of petals and of flattened ovaries and capsules. This is FLOPO obcordate.

target: new: conjunction of two values on the margin (region of the bearer: margin + scarious FLOPO:0991047 and ciliated PATO_0001408)
reason: The margin is both dry and papery (scarious) and fringed with hairs (ciliate), so both values hold. This follows scarious-margined and pilose-ciliate.

target: new: two values of one bearer (scaly PATO_0001804 + silvery colour of the scales, FLOPO:0988009 white)
reason: Lepidote means covered with scales (C235, scaly), and the scales are silvery. The colour belongs to the scales, and silvery maps to the white backbone colour in config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv.

target: brown (PATO_0000952)
reason: A light wash of brown on the part, handled like purple tinged and rose-tinged.

The meaning changes with the part. In wood, heterogeneous rays are made of two kinds of cells; a heterogeneous indumentum mixes hair types; for rhizomes the meaning is unclear. No single quality covers all of these.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023 + purple PATO_0000951)
reason: A purplish colour at the tip of the petal, floret or fruit. It is handled like black-tipped and brown-tipped.

target: new: conjunction of two values (sinuate FLOPO:0991113 and dentated PATO_0001205)
reason: The margin is wavy and also has small teeth, so both values hold. This is the same as repand-denticulate.

target: scaly (PATO_0001804)
reason: Covered with tiny scales, the same reading as squamulose, which was mapped to PATO scaly.

target: docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md (angular PATO_0001977)
reason: Somewhat angular: angular with the qualifier 'sub', like suborbicular and subrhombic.

target: new: wall of the bearer (part of the bearer, slot 1) + decreased thickness (PATO_0000592)
reason: A spelling variant of thin-walled. What is thin is the wall of the cell or part, so the wall is the bearer.

label: doubly crenate
definition: A scalloped quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing rounded teeth that are themselves crenate.
reason: Bicrenate is a synonym of doubly crenate, which was already proposed as a new class in an earlier batch of this review. It should be merged into that class, not made a second time.

target: streaked (FLOPO:0991206)
reason: Marked with short lines of another colour, which is FLOPO streaked. When the colour of the dashes is given, it goes on the marks, as with purple-streaked.

label: papilionaceous
definition: A zygomorphic quality inhering in a flower or corolla by virtue of its five petals being differentiated into an upper standard, two lateral wings and two lower petals joined or cohering to form a keel, as in the flower of a pea.
reason: A standard, well-defined corolla type in legumes. Zygomorphic alone loses the standard, wings and keel. The 'receptacle papilionaceous' example is a transcription error and should go on the corolla.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: rhomboid PATO_0001938 – hexagonal PATO_0002509)
reason: A compound of two shapes, read as a range between them, like rhombic-elliptic.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: spike-like FLOPO:0991142 – raceme-like FLOPO:0991197)
reason: A raceme so short-stalked that it approaches a spike: a range between the two inflorescence forms, like racemose-paniculate.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: ovate FLOPO:0991024 with value_qualifier 'sub' per docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md – lanceolate PATO_0001877)
reason: A range from ovate to lanceolate, as in ovate-lanceolate, with the first value marked 'sub' (approximate).
